title: Access Control — User Manual
summary: How to register Hikvision ISAPI door controllers, manage doors and credentials, and review the access event log.

sections.body:
Overview

Access Control manages physical door controllers over the Hikvision ISAPI protocol, across seven tabs: Manage Doors, Devices & Doors, Persons, Access Group, Credentials, Event Log, and ZigBee. This is a real hardware integration — actions here talk directly to the physical controller, not a simulation.

Key Features

  • Devices & Doors — register a controller by IP/port and credentials, run Test Connection (ISAPI) to confirm it's reachable, then add its doors. Each door has Open/Close for momentary control, plus a "More..." menu for Always Unlock, Always Lock (both override the door into a held state), and Resume Schedule (cancels the override and hands control back to the door's own schedule).
  • Credentials — provision an access card/employee number for a Person (from the Persons directory — a Person represents a physical building occupant and is separate from an app-login User) on a controller, with an optional valid-from/valid-to window and per-door access (mirroring Hikvision's own RightPlan): tick which doors a person may use and, for each, a schedule template number already configured on that controller (e.g. "1" = All-day, "2" = Weekday — this app assigns template numbers, it doesn't author the templates themselves). Leaving no doors ticked leaves the controller's own default access behavior in place. Provisioning calls the physical controller first; the local record is only saved if the controller accepts it, so the app never drifts ahead of what the hardware actually has enrolled.
  • Event Log — access events (opens, closes, denied attempts) pulled from the controller. The app doesn't expose a public webhook for the controller to push to — instead, use Sync Now on a device to pull its latest events on demand.

Step-by-Step

  1. In Devices & Doors, click Add Device and enter the controller's name, IP address, port, username, and password. Optionally set its Location (shared with Assets, Stock, and NVRs/Cameras).
  2. Run Test Connection (ISAPI) to confirm the app can reach the controller before relying on it.
  3. Add the physical doors wired to that controller.
  4. In Credentials, provision a card or employee number, tick the doors that person may use and set each door's schedule template number, with an optional validity window.
  5. Use the remote open/close controls on a door when needed, and Sync Now in Event Log to pull its latest access history.

Manage Doors

The Manage Doors tab shows every door as a tile with live open/closed and locked/unlocked state, refreshing automatically. Click a door tile to open an action popover with Open, Close, Remain Unlocked, Remain Locked, and Resume Schedule — the same controls available in bulk from the toolbar (tick the checkbox on a tile, which does not open the popover, to bulk-select doors first).

Persons & Organizations

The Persons tab is a directory of physical building occupants, organized into a tree of Organizations (departments/sites) on the left. A Person is not the same as an app-login User — most people with a door credential never log into this app at all. Click a person to open their profile across tabs: Basic Information, Credential (enroll cards here), Access Control, Resident Info, and Extension Info.

Access Group

An Access Group bundles a schedule template with a set of Persons and a set of doors, so you can grant the same access to many people at once instead of provisioning each person's doors individually. Create a group, pick its persons and access points (doors), then click Apply to push that access to the physical controllers — it loops every person × door pair and applies best-effort, so one unreachable device doesn't block the rest of the group from being applied.

ZigBee (Scaffold)

The ZigBee tab is a framework for future ZigBee-based access hardware (contact sensors, locks) — like Lighting's ZigBee tab, it is not a working integration yet: no coordinator hardware or radio stack is wired up in this build, and "Test Connection" will always report a clear failure rather than fake success until real hardware support is added.

Tips

  • Schedule template numbers ("1", "2", ...) must already exist on the controller itself before you reference them here — this app assigns a door to a template number, it doesn't create the underlying weekly schedule. Check the controller's own web admin page for which numbers are configured.
  • A failed Test Connection almost always means the IP, port, or credentials are wrong — double-check them against the controller's own web admin page before troubleshooting further.
